questions.q: In the AP chain, what are the two separate branches hanging off AP_INVOICES_ALL?
options: Business units and ledgers
Supplier identity and customer identity
Lines/distributions (accounting) and invoice payments (money-matching)
Journal headers and journal lines
questions.explain: One branch (lines and distributions) explains what was billed and how it's accounted; the other (AP_INVOICE_PAYMENTS_ALL) tracks how much has actually been paid — independently.

questions.q: Why can an AP invoice be fully posted to the General Ledger before it has been paid?
options: Because the accounting branch (lines/distributions) and the payment branch are independent of each other
Because AP_INVOICES_ALL has no accounting data
Because GL only accepts paid invoices
It can't — posting and payment always happen simultaneously
questions.explain: Accounting (distributions feeding Subledger Accounting and GL) and payment application are separate, independent branches off the invoice header.

questions.q: What is the structural equivalent, on the Receivables side, of AP's lines/distributions branch?
options: HZ_PARTIES
GL_LEDGERS
AR_CASH_RECEIPTS_ALL
RA_CUSTOMER_TRX_LINES_ALL
questions.explain: RA_CUSTOMER_TRX_LINES_ALL plays the same structural role as AP_INVOICE_LINES_ALL: explaining what a transaction's total is made of.

questions.q: What three ideas repeat across both the AP and AR chains?
options: Party, account, site
A header carrying the total, lines explaining what it's made of, and a separate money-matching table
Ledger, period, balance
Business unit, data access set, role
questions.explain: Both chains reduce to the same three structural ideas, just with different table names and vocabulary.

questions.q: Why is it risky to answer "is this transaction settled" using only a single flag on the header row?
options: Because this is never a risk — header flags are always perfectly reliable
Because header flags never exist in Oracle Fusion
Because money-matching lives in a separate branch (payments or receivable applications), so the real answer requires joining into that branch and checking amounts
Because headers never have any columns at all
questions.explain: Since the money-matching detail is structurally separate from the header, a cached header-level flag can be stale or incomplete — joining into the money-matching tables is the reliable approach.
